toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
Turnaround doubled mainly because of a control change on 1 April. Following an audit finding, adjusters' settlement authority was cut from $10,000 to $2,500. Claims of $2,500–$10,000 (about 53% of closures) now need a team-lead approval. Time pending approval for that band rose from 0.7 to 16 days. Its total went from 10.4 to 26 days. Other bands are flat. The three team leads receive about 212 items a week, against 38 before, and approve about 199. The approval backlog grew from 11 to 455 items. The change record says no workload assessment was done.

The hail surge ended by June (claim volumes are back to normal). Adjuster headcount was restored by June. Per-stage times for investigation and indexing are flat, which argues against the staffing and Quillfast explanations. Complaint counts rose partly because of a logging change.

Recommendation: do not sign for four contractors or an imaging switch. Work with Internal Audit to add approval capacity. For example, certify experienced senior adjusters as second approvers. Keep a second review on every claim in the band and track approval wait weekly. Don't discipline the team leads. Don't make the limit permanent until the December re-test. Confidence is high.
